[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for jumping on, uh quick roll call?

[00:28] Owen: quick note before we start, there are two versions of the run: hosted endpoint with auto-batching and a dedicated pool run with pinned GPUs. The baseline is the in-house cluster you ran last week   right?
[00:38] Lena: yeah baseline is our in-house k8s cluster with NVIDIA A100s, we ran their stock model and a quantized run. Might be called "baseline cluster" in the spreadsheet.
[00:46] Maya: great  ok first slide, p50 latency numbers: Redwood hosted p50 55ms vs baseline 72ms for the same 512-token workload, so about 20% better on p50.
[00:58] Marta: wait, 55ms that seems low, are we sure same sequence length and no extra pre/post processing?
[01:04] Owen: good question  the run strips client-side pre-processing in both; sequence length =512, beam=1, identical prompts, we used prefix caching where applicable. There may be slight differences in tokenizer versions but not material.
[01:16] Rahul: for throughput, baseline achieved 4500 tokens/s sustained at batch size 8, Redwood dedicated got 4300 tokens/s, hosted got 3600 tokens/s due to multi-tenant headroom.
[01:29] Lena: so baseline still wins on throughput for mid-size batches?
[01:33] Owen: for that exact hardware profile yes, baseline's cluster has a custom kernel path they tuned. But when we increased batch to 16 with quantized model Redwood dedicated jumped to 6800 tokens/s and baseline to 7000 tokens/s, so comparable.
[01:48] Maya: i'd flag p95 and p99 next  p95 on hosted was 210ms, p95 baseline 190ms; p99 baseline had some long tails at 900ms in their runs, which they traced to noisy neighbor interference.
[02:02] Rahul: we did see a tail when we had a cron job on a subset of nodes, yeah that could explain it.
[02:08] Lena: is the Redwood p99 stable with dedicated?
[02:11] Owen: dedicated is much more stable  p99 dropped to 320ms for the same config, so big improvement over hosted.
[02:18] Marta: what about cold-starts and KV cache warmup? baseline had a faster cold-start in some cases.
[02:24] Owen: baseline's cold-start wins because their serving process preloads the full KV cache at container start; our runtime warms KV progressively but we can provide prewarm hooks in Dedicated to match.
[02:34] Lena: can you also run a test with longer context lengths, 1024? our use-case sometimes bursts to 1k.
[02:40] Maya: yes we'll add 1024 runs  good call.
[02:43] Owen: about quantization, when we applied 4-bit q4 on Redwood dedicated, the throughput jumped ~1.6x vs fp16 and latency p50 dropped ~18ms, quality checks on our small eval set looked ok but we need your domain prompts.
[02:57] Lena: our legal/compliance folks worry about quantized models changing outputs; we'll need to see eval diffs.
[03:04] Maya: absolutely  we'll include delta logs and a diff of answers on your prompt set.
[03:09] Rahul: network egress was also a question  when we tried hosted we saw slightly higher jitter, is that purely network?
[03:16] Owen: yes hosted routes through regional gateways, if you want VPC-private Dedicated there won't be egress hops. For hosted we can pin region to reduce jitter.
[03:24] Marta: any SOC2 or audit logs differences between hosted and private?
[03:28] Jin: hosted has standard audit logs and is SOC2 compliant; Dedicated and Private add customer-managed KMS, more retention windows and can export full request/response logs to your SIEM.
[03:38] Lena: perfect  we'll need the security pack and SOC2 certs.
[03:41] Maya: we'll send the security deck after the call.
